subject: general
question: In an election between two candidates, 96% of the registered voters cast their vote and 15% of the votes polled were found invalid. The winning candidate got 80% of the valid votes and won the election by a margin of 1224 votes. How many voters were registered?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let total registered voters be T.

Valid votes = T × 96% × (100 − 15)% = T × 0.96 × 0.85

Winning margin = Valid votes × (80% − 20%) = Valid votes × 60%

⇒ T × 0.96 × 0.85 × 0.60 = 1224

⇒ T × 0.4896 = 1224 ⇒ T = 2500

**∴ The correct answer is 2500 voters.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Votes polled = 96% of registered voters

Invalid votes = 15% of polled votes

Winning margin = 1224 votes, Winner got 80% of valid votes

**Formula Used:**

Valid Votes = Total Polled × (100 − Invalid%)

Margin = Valid Votes × (Winner% − Loser%)

 
 Registered (100x)

 
• 
 96% voted

 Winner (65.28x)

 Margin = 65.28x − 16.32x = 48.96x = 1224

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the total registered voters be 100x.

⇒ Votes polled = 96% of 100x = 96x

⇒ Valid votes = (100 − 15)% of 96x = 85% of 96x = 81.6x

⇒ Winner's share = 80% of valid votes

⇒ Loser's share = (100 − 80)% = 20% of valid votes

⇒ Winning margin = (80% − 20%) = 60% of valid votes

⇒ Margin = 60% of 81.6x = 0.60 × 81.6x = 48.96x

⇒ Given margin = 1224

⇒ 48.96x = 1224 ⇒ x = 25

⇒ Total registered voters = 100x = 100 × 25 = 2500

**∴ The correct answer is 2500 voters.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Election Base Change Rule

In election problems, always track the base carefully. Invalid votes reduce the base of polled votes, and the winner's percentage is calculated on this new reduced base (valid votes).

Winning Margin Percentage

If there are only two candidates and one gets X% of the valid votes, the other automatically gets (100 − X)%. The winning margin in percentage is always (2X − 100)% of the valid votes.

Successive Percentage Trick

When multiple fractional changes occur sequentially, the final value can be written in a single step using multiplying factors: Final = Initial × (P₁/100) × (P₂/100) × (P₃/100).
